<!--
A guard on something apaquarto borrows from pandoc rather than a bug that
was fixed. citeprocr.lua takes the 's and & suffixes off a narrative
citation and records which it saw in the citation's hash field, an
undocumented field of pandoc's Citation; apaandcite.lua reads it back after
citeproc has run to write the possessive and to leave the ampersand alone.
If a pandoc or quarto upgrade stops hash surviving citeproc, nothing fails:
every citation below simply comes out plain, "Austen (1814/1990)" and
"Schneider and McGrew (2018)". The expectations say what each should be.
-->

Possessive: @austenMansfieldPark1990 ['s] novel.

Plain narrative, two authors: @schneiderCattellHornCarrollTheoryCognitive2018 said so.

Ampersand kept: @schneiderCattellHornCarrollTheoryCognitive2018 [&] said so.

Both: @schneiderCattellHornCarrollTheoryCognitive2018 ['s, &] account.
